brief: A PLA L-bracket 60 mm wide, made of 2 mm thick plate. The base leg is 50 mm long and lies flat; the upright leg stands on the back end of the base and is 40 mm tall overall. Two 10 mm holes pass through the base, 20 mm apart across its width, centred 25 mm from the front end. Two 5 mm holes pass through the upright, 20 mm apart across its width, centred 25 mm above the bottom. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

requirements.statement: The bracket is 60 mm wide overall.
requirements.rationale: Brief states overall width of 60 mm, uniform across base and upright.

requirements.statement: The base leg, lying flat, is 50 mm long, setting the part's overall depth.
requirements.rationale: The base leg length is the part's full extent in the direction it lies flat (Y), since the upright stands on its back end and adds no further depth.

requirements.statement: The bracket is 40 mm tall overall.
requirements.rationale: Brief states the upright leg is 40 mm tall overall, which is the whole part's height since the upright is the tallest feature.

requirements.statement: The plate (base and upright) is 2 mm thick.
The two holes through the base are 10 mm in diameter.
The two base holes are 20 mm apart across the base's width.
The base holes are centred 25 mm from the front end of the base leg.
The two holes through the upright are 5 mm in diameter.
The two upright holes are 20 mm apart across the upright's width.
The upright holes are centred 25 mm above the bottom of the upright.
Exactly two holes pass through the base leg.
requirements.rationale: Brief specifies two 10 mm holes through the base.

requirements.statement: Exactly two holes pass through the upright leg.
requirements.rationale: Brief specifies two 5 mm holes through the upright.

requirements.statement: The part shall have 2 open holes of 10 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

requirements.statement: The part shall have 2 open holes of 5 mm.
requirements.rationale: The brief sizes and counts these holes.

assumptions.statement: Each pair of holes (base and upright) is centred as a pair on the 60 mm width, i.e. symmetric about the part's midline, since only the 20 mm spacing between them is given and not their offset from the edges.
assumptions.rationale: The brief gives spacing between holes but not their lateral placement relative to the edges; centring the pair on the width is the conventional default for a symmetric bracket.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Holes would be offset from the intended mating pattern, misaligning the bracket with its mating part.

assumptions.statement: The junction between the base and upright legs is a sharp 90-degree bend with no additional fillet radius or gusset beyond what is implied by the plate thickness.
assumptions.rationale: Brief describes the upright as 'standing on the back end' of the base without specifying a fillet, radius or gusset.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A stress concentration at the corner could matter if the bracket is ever loaded, though currently no load case applies.

assumptions.statement: The part is modelled in generic PLA with no specific grade, infill or print orientation called out, since the brief only names the material as PLA.
assumptions.rationale: No load case applies, so material grade specifics (infill %, print orientation) have no functional consequence for this design.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: If the part is later loaded or exposed to heat, generic PLA properties may not be representative of the actual printed part.

assumptions.statement: The bracket operates in ordinary indoor ambient conditions, with no elevated temperature or outdoor/UV exposure.
assumptions.rationale: Nothing in the brief suggests harsh environmental exposure; PLA's low heat tolerance makes this a material default assumption.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: PLA softens near 50-60 degC and degrades under UV/humidity; an outdoor or heated application would invalidate the design.

assumptions.statement: All four holes are drilled straight through their respective leg faces, perpendicular to that leg's flat face.
assumptions.rationale: Brief states holes 'pass through' the base and upright, implying perpendicular through-holes for fasteners.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: Angled holes would change fastener alignment and mating geometry significantly.

notes: dropped 1 load question(s): the brief states that this part carries no load, so there was nothing to be uncertain about

added REQ_HOLES_10MM: the brief states 2 open holes of 10 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

added REQ_HOLES_5MM: the brief states 2 open holes of 5 mm, counted on the built part by diameter. A claim bound to a hole's parameter passes whenever some hole reads that parameter -- a collar had both set screws drawn at the bore's 12 mm, and no bore, and it passed.

document.name: L-shaped mounting bracket
document.description: A 2 mm PLA L-bracket: a 50 mm flat base leg and a 40 mm tall upright leg, 60 mm wide overall, each carrying a pair of mounting holes. Built flat then bent 90 degrees at the junction, per sheet-bending convention.

parameters.description: Overall width, shared by base and upright
Upright leg height overall, including the base thickness
Upright leg's own length before bending, so overall height after the bend is upright_height_overall
Total length of the unrolled flat plate before bending
Distance from the base leg's front end to the hole pair's centre
Distance from the upright's bottom (the bend line) to the hole pair's centre
Inside bend radius at the base-to-upright junction; no fillet/gusset beyond this called out in the brief

features.description: The whole bracket, unrolled flat: base leg from y=0 to base_length, upright leg continuing from y=base_length to flat_length. Width in X, length in Y, thickness in Z -- explicit axis mapping, no reordering by lies
First of two base mounting holes, through the plate's thickness
Second of two base mounting holes, through the plate's thickness
First of two upright mounting holes, drilled flat (perpendicular to the unbent plate's face) before the bend, measured from the bend line at base_length
Second of two upright mounting holes, drilled flat before the bend
Bends the upright leg up 90 degrees at the junction, holding the base leg fixed in place
